2608.23029.title: Meta-Moderator: Empowering Multi-Agent Debate with Meta-Cognition
2608.23029.paper_summary: Multi-agent debate can improve large language model reasoning by eliciting diverse hypotheses and critiques, yet its performance is often constrained by weak moderation. Common pipelines rely on fixed budgets, agreement-based stopping, or untrained judges, leading to redundant deliberation and unreliable evidence aggregation. We cast moderation as a meta-cognitive process, monitoring debate utility, controlling deliberation, and adjudicating a final answer, and introduce Meta-Moderator, a learnable framework that dynamically regulates debate and decides when to finalize an answer. Meta-Moderator is trained independently of the debaters via outcome-driven policy optimization, making debate regulation an explicit capability rather than an incidental effect of prompting. Across five benchmarks, Meta-Moderator outperforms widely used decision layers and transfers across tasks and system configurations. Further analyses show that it allocates debate more selectively and reduces mis-aggregation after informative hypotheses appear.
2608.23029.paper_summary_zh: 多代理辯論可以通過引出多樣的假設和批評來改善大型語言模型的推理，但其表現往往受到薄弱的調節限制。常見的流程依賴於固定預算、基於一致性的停止或未經訓練的評判者，導致冗餘的討論和不可靠的證據聚合。我們將調節視為一種元認知過程，監控辯論的效用，控制討論，並裁定最終答案，並引入Meta-Moderator，一個可學習的框架，動態調節辯論並決定何時最終確定答案。Meta-Moderator通過以結果為驅動的政策優化獨立於辯論者進行訓練，使辯論調節成為一項明確的能力，而不是提示的偶然效果。在五個基準測試中，Meta-Moderator的表現超過了廣泛使用的決策層，並在任務和系統配置之間轉移。進一步的分析顯示，它更具選擇性地分配辯論，並在出現有信息的假設後減少錯誤聚合。
